ip_top_stories.title: Sony Music and Warner Chappell Sue Anthropic, Allege 'Brazen Campaign' of Copyright Theft
ip_top_stories.summary: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell Music have filed a major lawsuit against Anthropic, alleging the AI company engaged in a 'brazen campaign' of intellectual property theft by using copyrighted song lyrics to train its Claude AI models without authorisation. The publishers are seeking billions in damages. The suit follows a $1.5 billion settlement Anthropic reached separately and represents one of the most significant music copyright actions against an AI company to date.

ip_top_stories.title: Carl Sagan Rights Holder Sues Luma AI Over 'Cosmos' Voice Clip in Ad
ip_top_stories.summary: The estate or rights holder of Carl Sagan has filed suit against Luma AI over the unauthorised use of a voice clip from 'Cosmos' in an advertisement. The case raises questions about AI companies' use of protected audiovisual and voice material for commercial purposes.

ip_top_stories.title: Can copyright subsist in works "authored" by AI? Federal Court to answer in CIPPIC v. Sahni
ip_top_stories.summary: A Canadian Federal Court is set to rule on whether copyright can subsist in works generated by AI, in the case of CIPPIC v. Sahni. The decision could have significant implications for how AI-generated content is treated under copyright law in Canada and potentially influence other jurisdictions.

ip_top_stories.title: The Underappreciated Third U.S. Fair Use Factor in Copyright Infringement Cases Concerning AI Training
ip_top_stories.summary: A legal analysis examines the third fair use factor — the amount and substantiality of the portion used — as an underappreciated consideration in U.S. copyright infringement cases involving AI training data. The piece argues this factor could play a more significant role in shaping litigation outcomes than current commentary suggests.

ip_top_stories.title: Goodbye Dolly
ip_top_stories.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen publishes an analysis under the title 'Goodbye Dolly', examining developments in AI and academic publishing with implications for intellectual property and the future of scholarly content.

ip_further_links.title: Edmonton rapper finds 129 of his songs in datasets used to train AI
ip_further_links.summary: A Canadian rapper discovered 129 of his songs included in AI training datasets without his consent, highlighting ongoing concerns among artists about unlicensed use of their work.

ip_further_links.title: 'It's high-tech theft': As AI music booms, Canadian artists demand consent, transparency and pay
ip_further_links.summary: Canadian musicians are calling for consent, transparency and remuneration as AI-generated music proliferates on streaming platforms, with artists citing unlicensed use of their recordings in AI training.

ip_further_links.title: How massive data pools remove the "smoking gun" of AI training
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis explores how the aggregation of vast datasets in AI training makes it increasingly difficult for plaintiffs to identify and prove specific instances of copyright infringement.

ip_further_links.title: Protect Creative Work: AI Petition Passes 10,000 Signatures
ip_further_links.summary: A petition calling for the protection of creative works from unlicensed AI training has surpassed 10,000 signatures, reflecting growing public and industry pressure on policymakers.

ip_further_links.title: Indian Publishers Conference 2026 Charts Roadmap for Copyright, AI and the Future of Publishing
ip_further_links.summary: The Indian Publishers Conference 2026 addressed the intersection of AI, copyright and the future of publishing, setting out a roadmap for the industry to navigate emerging digital challenges.

ip_further_links.title: Navigating AI Ownership in Commercial and License Agreements: Key Considerations for Technology Providers and Customers
ip_further_links.summary: A legal explainer outlines key considerations for technology providers and customers when addressing AI ownership and intellectual property rights in commercial and licensing agreements.

ip_further_links.title: Six Month Sales Rose, Profits Slipped at PRH [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: Penguin Random House reported that sales rose but profits slipped over the first six months of the reporting period, according to Publishers Weekly.
